# Total count strategies for paginated UIs — facts

## How it works

- [statement] When a UI needs the exact number of documents matching its active filters, use `countDocuments(filter)` independently of the page fetch. MongoDB defines it as counting query matches, and Mongoose's pagination example runs `find(filter)` and `countDocuments(filter)` in parallel. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.countDocuments/ · keywords: Total count strategies for paginated UIs · also: https://mongoosejs.com/docs/queries.html, https://github.com/Automattic/mongoose/blob/master/docs/queries.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/crud/query/count.md
- [statement] For sequential cursor or keyset interfaces, an exact total is optional: cursor pagination does not track a page position, and computing a separate exact count adds work. A continuation cue or approximate total can suit feeds and load-more UIs; offset pagination remains useful when users need arbitrary page jumps. (high confidence) — https://mongoosejs.com/docs/queries.html · keywords: Total count strategies for paginated UIs · also: https://blog.openreplay.com/pagination-patterns-mongodb/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] `estimatedDocumentCount()` reads collection metadata and does not accept a query filter. It is faster than an accurate count, so it can provide a rough unfiltered collection total but cannot provide the filtered total for a search or list view. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.estimatedDocumentCount/ · keywords: Total count strategies for paginated UIs · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/crud/query/count.md, https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-mongodb-index-for-count-operations/markdown
- [statement] $facet can return a page branch and a count branch from the same aggregation input. The page branch's $skip/$limit does not cap the count branch, which must count all documents that pass the preceding filter; one aggregation request therefore does not make an exact total free. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/facet.md · keywords: Total count strategies for paginated UIs · also: https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-mongodb-paginate-aggregation-results/view, https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/why-is-facet-so-slow/298075, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/facet/
- [statement] MongoDB limits each `$facet` stage's result to 100 MB, does not let `allowDiskUse` lift that limit, and still applies the 16 MiB BSON limit to the final output document. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/facet/ · keywords: Total count strategies for paginated UIs

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Published workload reports do not establish a universal latency winner between $facet and separate page/count operations: a .NET benchmark reported the separate path faster, its author reported $facet faster in a JavaScript shell, and a later test found the winner changed with whether its filter was indexed. Benchmark the actual pipeline, driver, and indexes. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/paging-with-count-performance-facet-vs-simple-query/170806 · keywords: Total count strategies for paginated UIs · also: https://www.reddit.com/r/mongodb/comments/1dym96r, https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/why-is-facet-so-slow/298075
- [statement] If the interface needs only a next-page indicator, request pageSize + 1 results, return the first pageSize, and set hasNext from whether the extra result exists. This avoids computing a full total and total-page count. (medium confidence) — https://stackoverflow.com/questions/21803290/get-a-count-of-total-documents-with-mongodb-when-using-limit/53220591 · keywords: Total count strategies for paginated UIs · also: https://www.linkedin.com/posts/ryad-lotfi-mahtal_search-api-mongodb-the-totalcount-trap-activity-7427312545063014400-RGwB, https://github.com/Automattic/mongoose/blob/master/docs/queries.md
- [statement] For a frequently read total over a well-defined subset, a cached or maintained counter can replace repeated counting, but writes must update it and the application should periodically reconcile it against the collection count. (medium confidence) — https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-mongodb-index-for-count-operations/markdown · keywords: Total count strategies for paginated UIs · also: https://www.reddit.com/r/mongodb/comments/13r8au0
- [statement] For an exact unfiltered collection count, `countDocuments({})` can perform a full collection scan. MongoDB documents an `_id_` index hint or an `_id >= MinKey` predicate as ways to use an index for this empty-filter case. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.countDocuments/ · keywords: Total count strategies for paginated UIs · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/crud/query/count.md
